### [Activating AI Safety Level 3 protections](https://www.anthropic.com/news/activating-asl3-protections)

**Anthropic** · 2026-11-13

Anthropic has provisionally activated AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) security and deployment standards for the release of Claude Opus 4 as a precautionary measure against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) risks.

- ASL-3 security standards enforce enhanced internal security measures to prevent sophisticated non-state attackers from stealing model weights.
- ASL-3 deployment standards focus on targeted safeguards to limit model misuse in acquiring or developing CBRN weapons while minimizing false-positive query refusals.
- Anthropic has not definitively determined if Claude Opus 4 meets the ASL-3 capability threshold, but activated the measures because CBRN-related risks could not be clearly ruled out.
- Evaluations ruled out ASL-4 requirements for Claude Opus 4 and confirmed that Claude Sonnet 4 does not require ASL-3 standards.

**Why it matters:** This marks the first time Anthropic has elevated a model's operational protections beyond the baseline ASL-2 standard to mitigate potential CBRN and weight-theft risks from increasingly capable AI models.

`ai-safety` `anthropic` `claude-opus-4` `cbrn` `cybersecurity`

### [Introducing Claude 3.5 Sonnet](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-5-sonnet)

**Anthropic** · 2026-11-13

Anthropic released Claude 3.5 Sonnet, a model outperforming Claude 3 Opus on key benchmarks at twice the speed, alongside Artifacts, a dedicated workspace feature for interacting with AI-generated content.

- Priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens with a 200K token context window.
- Operates at 2x the speed of Claude 3 Opus and set new benchmarks on GPQA, MMLU, and HumanEval.
- Solved 64% of problems in an internal agentic coding evaluation, compared to 38% by Claude 3 Opus.
- Surpasses Claude 3 Opus on vision benchmarks, improving chart interpretation and text transcription from imperfect images.
- Introduces Artifacts on Claude.ai, displaying code, documents, and designs in a dedicated side-by-side editing window.

**Why it matters:** Claude 3.5 Sonnet delivers frontier-level reasoning, vision, and coding capabilities at mid-tier latency and pricing, enabling more cost-effective multi-step workflows and agentic tasks.

### [Introducing the next generation of Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-family)

**Anthropic** · 2026-11-13

Anthropic released the Claude 3 model family—Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus—offering scaled capability options, improved speeds, multimodal vision support, and reduced incorrect prompt refusals.

- Opus outperforms peer models on benchmarks including undergraduate expert knowledge (MMLU), graduate expert reasoning (GPQA), and basic math (GSM8K).
- Haiku can process approximately 10k tokens of data-dense text and charts in under three seconds, while Sonnet operates at twice the speed of Claude 2 and 2.1.
- All three models incorporate sophisticated vision capabilities, allowing them to process photos, charts, graphs, technical diagrams, and PDFs.
- The model family shows a reduction in unnecessary refusals on boundary-testing prompts compared to prior Claude generations.

**Why it matters:** Developers and enterprise users can select models optimized for their specific balance of speed, cost, and intelligence while directly ingesting complex visual and non-English data.

### [Anthropic is endorsing SB 53](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-is-endorsing-sb-53)

**Anthropic** · 2026-11-13

Anthropic has formally endorsed California's SB 53, an AI governance bill introduced by Senator Scott Wiener that replaces prescriptive technical mandates with mandatory transparency and disclosure requirements for frontier AI developers.

- SB 53 adopts a 'trust but verify' framework focusing on disclosure requirements rather than prescriptive technical mandates.
- The legislation targets large companies building the most powerful frontier models, while exempting startups and smaller firms to avoid unnecessary regulatory burdens.
- The bill codifies voluntary industry practices, legally requiring covered developers to publish Responsible Scaling Policies (RSPs) and comprehensive system cards detailing model capabilities and safety risks.
- Anthropic supports SB 53 as a state-level baseline to prevent a 'race to the bottom' where labs might otherwise reduce safety disclosures to remain competitive.

**Why it matters:** The endorsement signals major lab alignment behind legally binding transparency standards, shifting AI regulation toward mandatory disclosures and Responsible Scaling Policies without imposing hard technical limits.

### [Build AI in America: Anthropic Energy Report](https://www.anthropic.com/news/build-ai-in-america)

**Anthropic** · 2026-11-13

Anthropic released its "Build AI in America" policy report, warning of energy capacity deficits and recommending policy reforms to secure at least 50GW of U.S. electric capacity for AI training and inference by 2028.

- Anthropic projects single advanced AI model training will require 2GW data centers in 2027 and 5GW data centers in 2028.
- Total U.S. frontier AI training energy demand is expected to hit 20-25GW by 2028, with an additional 25GW or more required for inference.
- The report highlights a domestic energy buildout lag behind China, which added over 400GW of power capacity last year compared to several dozen gigawatts added in the U.S.
- Proposed policy actions include establishing a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers nationwide permit for AI data centers under the Clean Water Act and creating strategic reserves of critical grid components and gas turbines.

**Why it matters:** Failure to rapidly scale domestic power generation and streamline permitting could cause the U.S. to lose its competitive lead in frontier AI development to China.

### [Challenges in red teaming AI systems](https://www.anthropic.com/news/challenges-in-red-teaming-ai-systems)

**Anthropic** · 2026-11-13

Anthropic released empirical insights and methodology details covering four distinct red teaming approaches for AI safety, transitioning from qualitative testing to quantitative automated evaluations.

- Evaluates four red teaming methodologies: domain-specific expert teaming, model-assisted red teaming, new modality red teaming, and open-ended general red teaming.
- Utilizes Policy Vulnerability Testing (PVT), an in-depth qualitative framework conducted with external subject matter experts to identify high-risk safety and policy threats.
- Addresses the lack of standardized AI red teaming practices, which currently hinders objective safety comparisons across different models.
- Outlines an iterative framework to convert qualitative adversarial findings into automated, quantitative safety evaluations.

**Why it matters:** Establishing standardized, multi-method red teaming practices is essential for benchmarking AI vulnerabilities and preparing safety evaluations for increasingly capable future models.
